abstract: OBJECTIVES: To characterize computed tomography (CT) features of fetus in fetu (FIF), correlate imaging findings with surgical and pathological results, and assess long-term outcomes, with emphasis on preoperative differentiation from teratoma. METHODS: We performed a retrospective imaging study of patients with surgically and pathologically confirmed FIF treated at a single institution. Clinical records, prenatal ultrasonography, postnatal CT examinations, operative findings, histopathology, and follow-up outcomes were reviewed, focusing on CT-demonstrated skeletal organization and relationships to adjacent organs and major vessels. Contrast-enhanced CT was available in 2 of the 7 patients (patients 1 and 4) and was primarily used to further evaluate lesion-vessel interfaces and relationships with adjacent organs. MRI was not routinely performed in this cohort and was not included in the primary imaging analysis. RESULTS: Seven patients (five females, two males) were included. Contrast-enhanced CT was available in two cases. Three lesions were detected prenatally on routine obstetric ultrasonography, and postnatal diagnosis ranged from the immediate neonatal period to 3 years of age. Lesions were predominantly retroperitoneal, with one patient presenting as an externally visible parasitic fetus beneath the xiphoid process. CT consistently demonstrated well-circumscribed, encapsulated masses containing fat and ossified skeletal elements. A vertebral axis was identified in two patients, whereas long bone or limb-like structures were observed in six. Several lesions showed close relationships with adjacent organs and major vascular structures, increasing surgical complexity. All patients underwent complete excision, and histopathology confirmed FIF in all cases. During long-term follow-up (1.3-10.4 years), no recurrence or malignant transformation was observed. CONCLUSIONS: CT is pivotal for diagnosing FIF by demonstrating organized skeletal architecture and defining anatomical relationships, enabling reliable differentiation from teratoma and supporting safe surgical planning with excellent long-term outcomes.
abstract_ja: 目的: 胎児内胎児(FIF)のCT所見を特徴づけ、画像所見を手術および病理結果と対応させ、長期転帰を評価すること。特に奇形腫との術前鑑別に重点を置いた。方法: 単一施設で手術および病理学的にFIFと確定した患者を対象とした後方視的画像研究を実施した。臨床記録、出生前超音波検査、出生後CT検査、手術所見、組織病理、経過観察の結果を検討し、CTで示される骨格構造と隣接臓器・主要血管との関係に焦点を当てた。造影CTは患者7例のうち2例(患者1と4)で利用可能であり、主に病変と血管の境界や隣接臓器との関係をさらに評価するために用いられた。本コホートでは日常的にMRIは施行されておらず、主要な画像解析には含めなかった。結果: 患者7例(女性5例、男性2例)を対象とした。造影CTは2例で利用可能であった。3病変は出生前の定期的な産科超音波検査で検出された。出生後の診断は、出生直後から3歳までの範囲であった。病変は主に後腹膜に発生し、1例は剣状突起の下に体外に見える寄生性胎児として現れた。CTでは、脂肪と骨化した骨格成分を含む、境界明瞭な被包性腫瘤が一貫して描出された。2例では椎体の軸が同定され、6例では長管骨または四肢様の構造が観察された。いくつかの病変は隣接臓器や主要血管と密接な関係を示し、手術の難易度を高めた。全例で完全切除が行われ、病理組織学的にすべての症例がFIFと確認された。長期経過観察(1.3〜10.4年)では、再発や悪性転化は認められなかった。結論: CTは、整然とした骨格構造を示し、解剖学的関係を明らかにすることでFIFの診断に決定的に重要であり、奇形腫との信頼できる鑑別を可能にし、安全な手術計画と優れた長期転帰を支持する。
